records.d: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered superconductivity in 1911: mercury losing all resistance at 4.2 Kelvin. The current flowed forever. The phenomenon was found.
records.h: Cooling mercury with liquid helium, resistance vanished abruptly. The discovery won the 1913 Nobel. The forever-current was real.
records.mj: Established - documented 1911 Onnes discovery; superconductivity in mercury.

records.d: Meissner and Ochsenfeld found in 1933 that superconductors expel magnetic fields: the levitating magnet. The effect was magnetic. The train would float.
records.h: The expulsion of flux enabled magnetic levitation. The physics was elegant. The float was real.
records.mj: Established - documented 1933 Meissner effect; flux expulsion.

records.d: Bardeen, Cooper, and Schrieffer published BCS theory in 1957: why superconductivity happens. The mechanism was Cooper pairs. The Nobel followed in 1972.
records.h: Electron pairing explained zero resistance. The theory was microscopic. The prize was shared.
records.mj: Established - documented 1957 BCS theory; 1972 Nobel Prize.

records.d: Brian Josephson predicted tunneling supercurrents in 1962: the Josephson junction. The effect enabled SQUIDs and qubits. The junction was the device.
records.h: Cooper pairs tunneling through barriers created precise devices. The applications were quantum. The Nobel came in 1973.
records.mj: Established - documented 1962 Josephson effect; 1973 Nobel Prize.

records.d: Nb3Ge hit 23.2 Kelvin in 1973: the conventional record that stood 13 years. The bar was 23K. The chase was on.
records.h: The A15 compound set the critical temperature record. The material was the limit. The chase continued.
records.mj: Established - documented Nb3Ge 23.2K; long-standing Tc record.

records.d: Bednorz and Muller found cuprate superconductivity at 35K in 1986: the ceramic surprise. The Nobel came in 1987. The revolution was ceramic.
records.h: Copper-oxide ceramics superconducted far above expectations. The discovery was shocking. The prize was fast.
records.mj: Established - documented 1986 cuprates; 1987 Nobel Prize.

records.d: YBCO superconducted at 92K in 1987: above liquid nitrogen's 77K. The coolant got cheap. The revolution went practical.
records.h: Yttrium barium copper oxide beat the nitrogen boiling point. The cooling was affordable. The applications opened.
records.mj: Established - documented 1987 YBCO; 92K superconductivity.

records.d: BSCCO reached 110K in 1988: the mercury-free high. The temperature climbed. The ceramics kept giving.
records.h: Bismuth strontium calcium copper oxide set new marks. The family grew. The climb continued.
records.mj: Established - documented BSCCO 110K; high-Tc progress.

records.d: Mercury cuprates hit 138K in 1993: the ambient-pressure record that still stands. The bar was set high. The record endures.
records.h: HgBaCaCuO set the highest ambient-pressure Tc. The record has stood 30+ years. The bar is 138K.
records.mj: Established - documented 138K Hg-cuprate; ambient-pressure Tc record.

records.d: Magnesium diboride superconducted at 39K in 2001: the simple surprise. The binary compound beat expectations. The cheap material worked.
records.h: The simple MgB2 showed 39K superconductivity. The material was cheap. The applications were practical.
records.mj: Established - documented 2001 MgB2; 39K superconductivity.

records.d: Iron-based superconductors found in 2008: the second high-Tc family. The iron age of superconductivity. The surprise was magnetic.
records.h: Iron pnictides superconducted despite magnetism. The family was new. The physics was rich.
records.mj: Established - documented 2008 pnictides; iron-based superconductors.

records.d: Hydrogen sulfide hit 203K under pressure in 2015: the hydride era began. The pressure was extreme. The temperature was high.
records.h: Diamond-anvil pressure made H2S superconduct at 203K. The hydrides were the path. The era was high-pressure.
records.mj: Established - documented 2015 H2S 203K; hydride superconductivity.

records.d: Lanthanum hydride hit 250K in 2019: near room temperature, under pressure. The goal was close. The pressure was the catch.
records.h: LaH10 superconducted near 250K at megabar pressures. The temperature was thrilling. The catch was pressure.
records.mj: Established - documented 2019 LaH10; ~250K under megabar pressure.

records.d: Nickelate superconductors found in 2019: the cuprate cousins. The family grew. The thin films worked.
records.h: Infinite-layer nickelates superconducted in thin films. The analogy was cuprate. The growth was epitaxial.
records.mj: Established - documented 2019 nickelates; new superconductor family.

records.d: A 2020 paper claimed room-temperature superconductivity in carbonaceous sulfur hydride: the announcement electrified, then collapsed. The retraction came in 2022. The lesson was verification.
records.h: The Dias claim of 288K superconductivity drew global attention. Replication failed. Nature retracted in 2022. The lesson was rigor.
records.mj: Established - documented 2020 claim and 2022 retraction; verification lesson.

records.d: LK-99 claimed room-temperature superconductivity in July 2023: the internet's superconductor summer. The videos went viral. The replication failed worldwide.
records.h: The Korean team's lead-apatite claim sparked massive replication. Labs worldwide found no superconductivity. The summer ended.
records.mj: Established - documented July 2023 LK-99 claim; worldwide replication failure.

records.d: The nitrogen-doped lutetium hydride claim was retracted in November 2023: the second Dias retraction. The field demanded rigor. The standard was replication.
records.h: Nature retracted the 2023 room-temp claim. The pattern was clear. The field moved on.
records.mj: Established - documented November 2023 retraction; room-temp claim withdrawn.

records.d: Hydride research continued in 2024: careful high-pressure work advancing. The science was sober. The progress was real.
records.h: Rigorous hydride studies refined understanding. The field was careful. The science was solid.
records.mj: Emerging - real research; ongoing high-pressure hydride studies.

records.d: Labs pursued ambient superconductors carefully in 2025: the hunts continue. The continue are the hunts. The 2025 is the pursued.
records.h: Replication standards tightened. The hunts are the continue. The pursued is the 2025.
records.mj: Emerging - real 2025 research; careful replication efforts.
